note: v1, written - the first round. EVERYTHING FALLS TO ONE: the Collatz rule as melody and form. Each phrase starts from a seed and a physical clarinet plays its path (n -> n/2 or 3n+1), one number an eighth at scale degree round(log2 n) on G major, so every climb is a melodic climb and every phrase - of its own irregular length - ends 4 2 1 = B3 A3 G3, the hook. Seeds 6 / 7 12 3 7 / 9 18 11 / 27 31 27 41 (27's 111-step climb to 9232 is the drop) / the loop 1 4 2 1. Tracker arps on a 5-bit chip, hats on the prime steps of every 32 (the sieve), an analog bass and a sine sub on I vi IV V, a dream-vox pad; a humanized voice on a radio reads 7's path aloud, and on the break 'four, two, one' turns from speech to song on the hook's own notes. 128 bpm, 164 bars, 310 s. compscore seeds 0/11: 93.46/91.55 (draft 87.6/87.7: spectrum 46 -> 83 from the body - the analog bass, the pad and arps an octave down, a 1.5 kHz dip; cohesion 31 -> 95; the outro keeps the band to its last beat to bleed into t3 - a fade read as a 42 dB drop). note: v14, written: THE CLIMB IS A REACH. The hailstone's two moves now sound different on the clarinet: every note the rule makes by 3n+1 (after an odd number) is scooped up into from a semitone below - bend=-1 for a 32nd, -0.5 for a 32nd, then home for the rest of the eighth (score tokens; the stream writes the scoop verbatim) - while the halvings fall plainly. The climbs strain, the falls are easy, and the 4-2-1 home stretch is all falls. The album's first use of bend. compscore seeds 0/11: v13 98.195/98.240 -> v14 98.222/98.262; scooping from two semitones read 98.21/98.23. Levels -11.0 LUFS, true peak -1.29 dBTP. note: v21, written (judgment keep, -0.02): THE BREAK IN THE CYCLE'S OWN METER - the album's first meter change. Every path ends in 4 -> 2 -> 1, a loop of three, so the break goes to 3/4 (tempo map: meter 3/4 at 304b, back to 4/4 at C, 364b; 20 bars of 3/4 = 60 beats against 16 of 4/4 = 64, so the record is 308.2 s). The voice now counts it like a waltz, an upbeat count: 'four' on beat 2, 'two' on beat 3, ONE on the next downbeat. The take's own lead-ins are kept; 'four'/'two' fit a beat (0.9), 'one' is held longer each pass (1.2 -> 2.6 beats) as the speech turns to song. The v19 bell's loop is turned (G4 G6 G5) so its 1 lands on the downbeat with the voice's, so the three-against-four polymeter of v19 becomes the meter itself.
